chunks: Aban, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The Mugheera are claiming that this day is for the approaching night.' He said: 'They lie! This day is for the night that has passed. Indeed, the people of Bani Nakhl, when they saw the crescent, said: The Sacred Month has entered.'

key_terms.الشَّهْرُ الْحَرَامُ: The Sacred Month, referring to one of the four months in which fighting was traditionally prohibited in pre-Islamic and Islamic Arabia.
key_terms.الْمُغِيرِيَّةَ: The Mugheera, a group or faction known in hadith literature, often associated with specific juristic opinions.
key_terms.الْهِلَالَ: The crescent moon, used for sighting to determine the beginning of lunar months.
key_terms.بَطْنِ نَخْلَةَ: Bani Nakhl, a tribe or clan mentioned as a reference point for the sighting of the crescent.

ai.seo_question: How does the Shia tradition determine the start of a lunar month based on crescent sighting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the Mugheera tribe's claim by establishing the principle of *tali al-layl al-nahar* (the day follows the night), confirming that the new day begins at sunset rather than midnight. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for lunar calendar calculations, emphasizing that the visibility of the crescent at sunset determines the start of the month, a view supported by the people of Bani Nakhl who declared the entry of the Sacred Month upon sighting. This ruling underscores the authority of local moon-sighting reports in determining religious obligations such as fasting and Eid.
